recipes.name: Three Bean Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
0.75 cup white sugar, or to taste

steps.text: Mix together green beans, wax beans, kidney beans, onion, sugar, vinegar, vegetable oil, salt, pepper, and celery seed. Chill in refrigerator for at least 12 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Three Bean Salad
raw_recipe.description: This three bean salad made with green beans, wax beans, and kidney beans keeps well, serves a lot of people, and is great for summer picnics and cookouts.

video.description: The tasty three bean salad in this video is great for buffets, summer picnics, and cookouts. It's easy to make but tastes best when chilled for at least 12 hours. It keeps well and serves a lot of people.
video.name: How to Make Three Bean Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together green beans, wax beans, kidney beans, onion, sugar, vinegar, vegetable oil, salt, pepper, and celery seed. Chill in refrigerator for at least 12 hours.

review.reviewBody: Good recipe, but I made a few changes - cut the sugar to 1/4 cup, added a small diced green bell pepper and used olive oil instead of vegetable oil. I also used fresh green beans that I cut in small pieces and boiled 2-3 minutes, then rinsed in cold water. You can also use chick peas instead of yellow beans. Let marinate overnight and mix a few times during this time. Bon appétit!

Made this with a few modifications. I added a can of garbanzo beans,I cut the sugar back to 1/4 cup, substituted half the oil with olive oil, substituted half the white vinegar for rice wine vinegar and added a drizzle of sesame oil. Everyone loved it! Next time I may cut the sugar a bit more.

Best recipe ever! The only change I make is adding one can red kidney beans, one can black beans and one can chick peas. This recipe provides the ideal base to add whatever you want! On its own it's perfect too!
Awesome! I doubled the recipe and still only use a 1/4 cup of sugar. It came out perfect

Shades of my mom's favorite. We grew up with this, and it's the first time I' very made it in years. Sweet & sour marinades are an individual flavor choice and this is a bit sweet for my crew. Definitely less sugar next time. Another suggestion from my own experience for a different twist: we used to occasionally add shoestring cut cooked beets to this bean mix, let it marinate overnight, drain it and add a spoonful of plain yogurt.

This is delicious- if you cut the sugar to 1/2 C. and add a big splash of apple Cider Vinegar AND let it set for a day....I didn't like it very well at first but let it set overnight and its delicious! I also added a pint of garbanzo beans.....

I used fresh frozen green beans and microwaved them. I also added 1 can northern white beans. I substiuted the celery salt and used 2 ribs fresh celery sliced fairly thin. I loved it and so did my guests.

Made salad with few changes/additions. Added only 2 -3 tablespoons finely diced red onion, 1/4 cucumber diced small along with 1/2 Red Bell Pepper and 1/4 Green Bell Pepper diced small. Made dressing exactly per recipe. Added additional salt, pepper, cayenne & good dose of Aleppo pepper for some heat. Outstanding after 24 hr marinating!

12.29.17 Haven’t made three bean salad in years, and we used to live on it when first married...for two people, it lasted a while! Actually, I think I lost my original recipe, so was happy to see this on the AR site. I did make a few changes. I used Orange Muscat Champagne Vinegar (I know, sounds pretty fancy for a bean salad and I sure didn’t use that when first married!) instead of the milder white viinegar, used Splenda® instead of sugar (cut that back to 1/2 cup), and reduced the oil to 1/4 cup. This was like a blast-from-the past, and I found myself eating it out of the mixing bowl, but eventually, I did put it in the fridge overnight for the flavors to meld. This was so tasty, and I’ve saved this in my Favorites, so it won’t be lost again.

We love this bean salad! I make it exactly as is in the recipe. except I use red onion to enhance the color. Sometimes, I add an extra bean because my sister likes 4-bean salad. Other than that, I get requests for it all the time. It reminds me of the bean salad my mom made when I was a kid from the 1950s on.
i cut sugar to 1/2 cup and boil vinegar and sugar together. toos in the onions to quick pickle and soften them.

We love the basic recipe but personalized it by adding different beans, fresh celery, frozen cut green beans, and frozen corn! Love the idea of adding chopped bell peppers, too! This has become a staple in the fridge for snacks, salads, and side dishes.
This recipe was WAY to sweet for my taste, to the point of wondering if there was a typo in the list of ingredients. Should it not be 3/8 C sugar instead of 3/4.
Substitute olive oil for any other you might use--same taste and better for you.
I did not add celery seed. Everything was great

Just like grandma's. You can cut back on the sugar and oil a bit if you like. It's just fine the way it is, but you can also add whatever you have on hand: chickpeas, thinly sliced celery or radishes, or even some diced boiled red potatoes.
Really love this recipe, but the amount of oil is too much. I've tweaked it to my own tastes and use it as a foundation recipe over and over again.
i make it a few times a week, and use it as a snack, or side dish
This salad very similar to my mother’s recipe. She does include the chickpeas, no oil, apple cider vinegar provides a stronger flavor, and small jar sliced mushrooms. Drain before serving.

I love this recipe , Eating salad every day is a healthy diet. I always recommend people eat a salad daily and I love trying different salads. Recently I tried Pita Chips with salad and It was awesome in taste. no one will hate this unique salad recipe. It gives you high protein and energy.
